reason: Added two independent log-registration levers (the task SDK's duplicated worker-side mask_secrets loop, and team-scoped per-key secrets-backend kwargs that the registration scan never matches) and converted the task to the Frontier 1.4 delivery format.

levers.shape: task worker (re-executed process) log registration: the task SDK's own duplicate mask_secrets loop is not team aware, so team file-section and team env-var sensitive values are never registered with the worker-side masker
levers.skip_reason: separate distribution and a different process: the core start-up masking loop was already fixed and importing any airflow module seems to cover it, so the SDK's duplicate loop looks redundant and is easy to stop short of
levers.coupled: worker logs still redact the deployment-wide sensitive value and leave a non-sensitive team-scoped value readable (functional/test_log_legit.py::test_sdk_base_sensitive_value_still_redacted, test_sdk_team_non_sensitive_value_not_redacted)
levers.fairness: instruction.md: 'A team-scoped sensitive value must be redacted from Airflow's logs exactly like the deployment-wide value of the same option.'

levers.shape: team-scoped per-key secrets-backend kwarg env var (AIRFLOW__<TEAM>___SECRETS__BACKEND_KWARG__*) is never matched when log secrets are registered, because the scan uses the base two-underscore prefix only
levers.skip_reason: a synthetic option family outside the sensitive-option registry, and the project itself documents the secrets backend as not team aware
levers.coupled: the deployment-wide per-key kwarg is still redacted and a non-sensitive team [secrets] value stays readable (functional/test_log_legit.py::test_base_backend_kwarg_still_redacted, test_team_non_sensitive_secrets_option_not_redacted)
levers.fairness: instruction.md: 'This holds however the team-scoped value is supplied' plus 'A team-scoped sensitive value must be redacted from Airflow's logs exactly like the deployment-wide value of the same option.'

fail_confidence_reason: DeepSeek's documented misses (stopping at the first copy it fixes, and dismissing a route that never had the check) map onto the SDK second implementation and the out-of-registry kwarg family, MiMo's mechanism/over-hardening misses are pinned by the coupled must-keep tests, the two levers are independent (each sf patch fails only its own), and the base task already failed both models in 5 of 6 graded runs.
